hero.title: San Bernardino
hero.subtitle: Lakeside living, mature greenery and genuine privacy—less than an hour from Asunción.

intro.title: A place to live differently
intro.text: San Bernardino lies on the shores of Lake Ypacaraí, forty-eight kilometres from Asunción. Its still water, mature trees and established residential character give it an identity entirely its own. Founded by German settlers in the 1880s, the town retains a distinct cultural heritage that remains visible today. Close enough to the capital when needed, yet far enough away for the pace to change.

experiences.title: Ordinary days, elevated by the setting

items.title: Sunsets over the water
items.description: At the close of day, Lake Ypacaraí reveals one of San Bernardino's defining qualities. Light, water and open horizon create an atmosphere of quiet distinction.

items.title: Clubs, sailing and social life
items.description: A long tradition of yacht clubs and watersports gives the town a social and sporting dimension valued by families, second-home owners and those drawn to an active life on the water.

items.title: Food with its own character
items.description: Restaurants, cafés and historic patisseries are part of the experience here. San Bernardino brings together German heritage, Paraguayan cuisine and contemporary dining in a relaxed, walkable setting.

distances.title: Everything close, when you need it

living.title: What to know before living in San Bernardino

items.title: Beaches and the lake
items.text: Lake Ypacaraí dominates the landscape. Its shoreline offers promenades, private clubs, town beaches and open-air spaces enjoyed throughout the year.

items.title: Shopping and services
items.text: The town offers supermarkets, pharmacies, medical centres and everyday convenience shopping, with efficient connections to the larger retail destinations of San Lorenzo and Asunción.

items.title: Festivals and social life
items.text: Throughout the summer, the town comes alive with concerts, cultural events, markets and festivals at venues including the José Asunción Flores Amphitheatre and Casa Hassler.

items.title: Where to eat
items.text: The dining scene ranges from traditional restaurants and cafés to German-heritage patisseries and contemporary venues that follow the rhythm of the season.

gastronomy.title: A food scene with its own character

items.name: Bistró Del Val
items.description: Thoughtfully prepared cuisine in an intimate setting, well suited to quiet dinners.

items.name: Café Francés
items.description: A local institution with European influence, valued for its cuisine and unhurried atmosphere.

items.name: La Alemana
items.description: A San Bernardino landmark, known for its baking and its connection to the town's German heritage.

market.title: A market with depth and direction
market.text: San Bernardino has neither been overdeveloped nor lost its character — rare for a lakeside town within an hour of a capital city. Shoreline land is finite, and demand from families choosing to live here year-round rather than seasonally continues to grow. Foreign buyers may acquire urban property in Paraguay without residency, subject to the appropriate legal, tax and title due diligence.
highlights: Full freehold ownership available to foreign buyers
